reference: Read-only CLI behavior is compared with the installed GNU util-linux chrt under the same isolated namespace; Bash type/help metadata is checked against Bash's builtin contract and the documented chrt synopsis in the pinned loadable source. No scheduler policy is changed.
coverage: Bash identifies chrt as a loadable builtin and help exposes its documented query/set synopsis and policy names.
GNU util-linux parity for short and long priority-bound query options.
Read-only scheduling policy/priority query for the fixture shell itself, with only its variable PID normalized.
Safe invalid PID and unknown-option errors (status, stdout, and nonempty diagnostic presence).
exclusions: No sched_setscheduler or sched_setattr operation is executed; changing a process scheduling policy is deferred to a disposable VM or syscall mock.
No --all-tasks, reset-on-fork, deadline parameter, or child-command scheduling behavior is exercised; the two deferred cases name the needed isolated fixtures.
The current-process query is read-only and does not cover behavior against other processes or thread groups.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must resolve chrt as a builtin, consistent with the loadable registration contract.
Bash help must expose the documented read-only PID query and both policy-setting forms.
cases.script:
doc=$(help chrt)
[[ $doc == *'chrt -p PID'* && $doc == *'chrt [policy] PRIO COMMAND [ARG...]'* && $doc == *'chrt [policy] --pid PRIO PID'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'query and policy forms documented\n'

cases.purpose: Bash help must document the supported policy selector spellings and their scheduler names.
cases.script:
doc=$(help chrt)
[[ $doc == *'Policy flags: -o/-b/-i/-f/-r/-d for OTHER/BATCH/IDLE/FIFO/RR/DEADLINE.'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'policy flags documented\n'

cases.purpose: Compare the non-mutating -m scheduler priority bounds query byte-for-byte with GNU util-linux chrt.
Check that --max is equivalent to the GNU util-linux priority-bounds query and is accepted by both implementations.
Compare the read-only -p query for the running fixture shell; normalize only the sandbox-specific PID so policy, priority, and any runtime fields remain checked.

An invalid PID operand must fail before any scheduler syscall; compare GNU status, stdout, and exact diagnostic bytes. Diagnostic presence is compared; shell prefixes and implementation-specific wording are excluded.
An unknown option is a safe parser error; compare status, stdout, and diagnostic bytes against GNU. Diagnostic presence is compared; shell prefixes and implementation-specific wording are excluded.
Exercise policy selection, priority boundaries, reset-on-fork, argv forwarding, and child exit-status propagation without changing host process scheduling.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with scheduling changes confined to disposable child processes, or an independently reviewed syscall mock for sched_setscheduler plus fork/exec/wait. The future fixture should cover OTHER/BATCH/IDLE/FIFO/RR, valid and invalid priorities, -R, command arguments, and child exit/signal status.

cases.purpose: Exercise existing-PID/all-thread policy changes and SCHED_DEADLINE parameter validation only against an isolated target.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a dedicated throwaway process/thread group and appropriate scheduling privilege, or a reviewed sched_setscheduler/sched_setattr mock. The future fixture should check -p PRIO PID, --all-tasks, deadline runtime/deadline/period constraints, reset-on-fork interactions, and failure behavior without targeting any host process.
